claims.wording: DiskFox is made by independent developer Krishan Assi; DiskFox is his trading name.
claims.excerpt: DiskFox is a trading name of Krishan Assi, a sole trader

claims.wording: Official release notes list DiskFox 1.2.2, dated 18 October 2026, for macOS 14+ on Apple silicon and Intel.
claims.excerpt: 18 October 2026 · macOS 14 or later, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
claims.conditions: Newest listed release in inspected source; not an installed build test.

claims.wording: The advertised one-time US price is $10.99, with sales tax where applicable; 1.2.1 lists £8.99 UK and €9.99 in euro countries.
claims.excerpt: New prices: DiskFox now costs £8.99 in the UK, $10.99 in the US and €9.99 in countries that use the euro.
claims.conditions: No checkout, payment or tax-total verification. Do not promise future-major upgrades or directory $10 price.

claims.wording: A paid licence covers up to two Macs, including business use, and every version 1 update; later major releases may be paid upgrades.
claims.excerpt: A paid licence can be active on up to two Macs at a time.
claims.additionalExcerpt: Your licence includes every update to version 1 of DiskFox at no extra cost.

claims.wording: The full-feature 14-day trial starts when chosen, can start once, needs no account/payment details and does not become a paid purchase automatically.
claims.excerpt: The trial starts only when you choose it, lasts 14 days, can be started once, and includes every feature.
claims.additionalExcerpt: The trial needs no account or payment details, and it never turns into a paid purchase.

claims.wording: DiskFox is commercial licensed software, not a verified open-source offer.
claims.excerpt: DiskFox is licensed, not sold. We, or our licensors, own all intellectual property rights in DiskFox. Your licence doesn't give you any other rights in it.
claims.conditions: Proprietary licence classification supported by restrictions; no public source repository verified.

claims.wording: The vendor documents scan baselines, comparison of completed scans and Likely labels for inferred causes, not definitive attribution.
claims.excerpt: DiskFox uses that metadata to build a baseline and compare completed scans.
claims.additionalExcerpt: Where DiskFox infers a cause rather than confirming it, it labels it "Likely" and shows how confident it is.

claims.wording: Removal requires review and confirmation. Default removal is to Trash, but selected permanent actions and Xcode-tool removals differ.
claims.excerpt: DiskFox never removes anything automatically. Recommendations stay proposals until you review the items affected and confirm.
claims.additionalExcerpt: Some Xcode simulator items are removed with Xcode's own tool rather than moved to the Trash.
claims.conditions: Not a risk-free or universally reversible claim. Permanent deletion requires typing DELETE per terms.

claims.wording: DiskFox documents storage regrowth alerts, storage trends and cleanup history.
claims.excerpt: Storage alerts warn you when something you watch grows back or goes over a limit you set.
claims.additionalExcerpt: Activity keeps Storage Trends and a Cleanup History of what moved and how free space changed.

claims.wording: The vendor says routine scans use metadata, duplicate verification reads contents locally, and file names/contents are not uploaded; updates, licence checks and default-on anonymous usage counts still use the network.
claims.excerpt: Three anonymous usage counts (opened, first scan, days used) are on by default. Switch them off in Settings › General.
claims.additionalExcerpt: Duplicate scans read files locally to verify exact matches. File contents never leave your Mac.
claims.conditions: Attributed published statements, not traffic audit. Not entirely offline or zero telemetry.

claims.wording: Full Disk Access and the administrator helper are optional; restricted locations can remain unmeasured.
claims.excerpt: Extra permissions, such as Full Disk Access, notifications or opening at login, are optional.

claims.wording: Vendor documentation says the direct download is Developer ID signed and Apple notarised, not a Mac App Store edition.
claims.excerpt: No. DiskFox is sold directly from this site.
claims.additionalExcerpt: The download is signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple.
claims.conditions: Vendor disclosure only; no independent signature or notarisation test.

claims.wording: DiskFox documents developer caches as well as app inspection and exact duplicates.
claims.excerpt: Clean Up now covers uv, Poetry, Bun and conda caches, and lists downloaded Hugging Face models one by one.
claims.conditions: Models are not selected initially; uv/conda use their tools. This does not prove compatibility with every cache version.

claims.wording: Some protected-file recovery guidance is unsupported by Apple and may require Recovery; DiskFox does not execute it.
claims.excerpt: These procedures are not documented or supported by Apple, can stop working after a macOS update, and may involve starting your Mac in macOS Recovery.
claims.conditions: Do not reproduce instructions to bypass system protection in this article.

claims.wording: Official product screenshots are real-app Demo Mode sample data, not measured savings.
claims.excerpt: No invented dashboards: every screen was captured from the real app in Demo Mode with sample data.

claims.wording: Breathing Room is a free Apache-2.0 macOS 13+ preview; optional hosted AI Care is advertised at $5 USD/month or $50 USD/year.
claims.excerpt: AI Care is advertised at **$5 USD/month or $50 USD/year**, not a separate app purchase.
claims.conditions: Reused same-day register: 0.1.0-preview.1, Apple Development signed, not Developer ID/notarised, Python 3.10+ required; physical Intel and clean-machine runtime unverified. Hosted AI requires authentication/internet and may receive relevant paths/process/storage information.

claims.wording: Breathing Room source implements grouped helper CPU/memory views, storage investigation, developer-cache discovery and activity history; this does not certify installer feature parity.
claims.excerpt: Native sampling groups helpers through parent/app relationships and exposes CPU/memory.
claims.conditions: Source-level claim only. Scheduled care requires app running and exact saved approvals; optional automatic mode is narrowly verified Ruff caches, not blanket review before every action.

claims.wording: DiskFox process/helper CPU-memory grouping and Python/runtime dependencies are not verified.
claims.conditions: Do not turn missing documentation into No or claim dependency-free installation.

workflow.title: Compare Mac storage scans without mistaking missing access for cleanup
workflow.primaryIntent: Interpret growth, incomplete scans and permission changes before deciding what to remove
workflow.descriptionDirection: Start with the conclusion: compare the same scope with consistent permissions, distinguish measured changes from likely causes, then review removal separately. No guaranteed attribution or savings.
outline: Place real DiskFox visual after lead, only when reuse cleared
Establish a baseline and record accessible locations; no hands-on claim
Why a permission gap must not become a negative-growth result: DiskFox 1.0.5 and 1.2.2 examples
Read measured growth separately from Likely causes
Review Trash, permanent and owning-tool actions; do not reproduce protected-file recovery steps
Compare recorded outcomes and watch regrowth; do not equate file size or Trash movement with available-space gain
Bounded choice: DiskFox documented storage history versus Breathing Room source-level app/helper activity and optional hosted investigation; disclose we build Breathing Room
workflow.distinctEvidence: DiskFox 1.0.5 preserves last measured size on access loss; 1.2.2 compares newly accessible folders with first readable scan, not an inaccessible baseline.
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a small decision checklist: same folder scope? same permission coverage? measured or inferred? Trash or permanent/tool action? No real filesystem access or invented calculator savings.
workflow.visualPlacement: DiskFox Home after lead; labeled Breathing Room Space preview at later decision section

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs DiskFox: storage history and app activity
comparison.intent: Choose between overlapping Mac storage tools based on documented workflow, maturity and hosting boundaries
comparison.format: Concise conclusion, claim-mapped matrix, who should choose each, limitations, workflow link and adjacent sources
comparison.recommendation: DiskFox fits readers seeking documented local scan history, exact duplicates, app footprint inspection and one-time licensing. Breathing Room, which we build, may fit readers evaluating source-implemented grouped app/helper activity and hosted assistance, subject to preview/runtime caveats. Do not claim one is safer, faster or universally cheaper.

diskfox: Documented history, likely-cause labels, receipts and regrowth alerts; these are not Breathing Room-only distinctions (D07/D09).
Commercial one-time two-Mac version-1 licence and vendor-declared notarised direct distribution (D03/D04/D12).
Local scan/duplicate processing but default-on anonymous counts and online licence/update connections (D10).
Permissions limit coverage, some recovery steps are unsupported by Apple, some removal is permanent/tool-driven; no measured performance comparison (D08/D11/D14).
breathingRoom: Free open desktop source and source-implemented grouped helper CPU/memory plus developer-cache inspection (B01/B02).
Optional hosted authenticated AI is not all-offline; ongoing AI Care price differs from DiskFox purchase, so compare needs, not bare sticker prices (B01).
Non-notarised preview, Python requirement and unverified clean-machine/Intel runtime must remain visible (B01).
